name: DIAPH1-related Sensorineural Hearing Loss-Thrombocytopenia Syndrome
aliases: Autosomal dominant sensorineural hearing loss with thrombocytopenia

criteria.description: Progressive sensorineural hearing loss typically presenting in childhood or early adulthood
Persistent thrombocytopenia with platelet counts below normal reference range
Identification of a pathogenic variant in the DIAPH1 gene
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of hearing loss and thrombocytopenia
Exclusion of other causes of sensorineural hearing loss and thrombocytopenia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive sensorineural hearing loss, thrombocytopenia, and a pathogenic DIAPH1 variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm diagnosis; clinical presentation may vary in severity.

laboratory: Persistent thrombocytopenia with platelet counts typically between 50,000-100,000/µL
Presence of macrothrombocytes on peripheral blood smear
imaging: Audiometry showing bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
Temporal bone MRI usually normal or nonspecific
genetic: Pathogenic heterozygous variants in the DIAPH1 gene (autosomal dominant inheritance)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant sensorineural hearing loss and thrombocytopenia

redFlags: Family history of early-onset deafness with bleeding tendency
references: OMIM Entry #615085 - DIAPH1-related sensorineural hearing loss and thrombocytopenia
Ueyama H, et al. DIAPH1 mutations cause sensorineural hearing loss and thrombocytopenia. Am J Hum Genet. 2011
